name: Cynanchum

project_scope.selection_mode: Master Plant Pool approved row 328 / My iNaturalist Flora row 266
related_excluded_concepts: Cynanchum racemosum sensu lato — do not duplicate
Cynanchum laeve — comparison only, not part of this one-species source pool selection
project_scope.note: 2023 FNA and current Kew POWO accept Cynanchum unifarium; older UT Williamson treatment retains varietal Cynanchum racemosum var. unifarium. No second card for the variety.

look_here_first: Start with the flowering AXIL of the vine, where a branched racemelike cluster of many TINY pale yellow-green flowers (white margins, ~5 mm across) emerges by an opposite leaf pair. A full heart-shaped leaf by itself could be Matelea, Gonolobus, or Cynanchum. Verify milky WHITE sap, a line of short hairs along the stem, and smooth PLUMP follicles if present.
shared_traits: Milkweed subfamily member within Apocynaceae; perennial twining vine with opposite leaves and milkweed gynostegium and pollinia.
Talayote (the local selected member) has abundant white latex, unlike the clear latex key character of C. laeve; not all Cynanchum share the same sap color.
Flowers individually small, pale green with white margins, clustered in racemelike axillary branching cymes.
Corolla lobes and corona hoods are distinct anatomical regions: green/white corolla lobes, with small fleshy three-lobed corona structures near the fused gynostegium.
Mature follicles plump and smooth; never confuse with rough Matelea pods or sharply angled Gonolobus fruits.

quick_key.if: Very small (~5 mm) pale green-and-whitish flowers in many-flowered axillary spray; heart-shaped opposite leaves; white latex; smooth inflated pod
Larger pale-green flat flowers densely NETTED dark green with silver 'pearl'; somewhat muricate pod
quick_key.then: Matelea reticulata — pearl milkvine, not Cynanchum

quick_key.if: Larger bell-shaped longitudinally LINED pale-green flower with hairy interior and five fleshy corona segments
quick_key.then: Matelea edwardsensis — plateau milkvine, not Cynanchum

quick_key.if: Uniform olive-green larger flowers, yellow anther appendages, strong ANGLES on otherwise smooth pod
quick_key.then: Gonolobus suberosus var. granulatus — anglepod, not Cynanchum

quick_key.if: Clear (not white) latex and white flowers; FNA narrower eastern concept
quick_key.then: Cynanchum laeve — comparison-only, not current source-pool card

comparison_cards.title: Talayote or pearl/plateau milkvine?
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Photograph the ENTIRE flower group before zooming. Talayote has a many-flowered, branched spray of TINY green-white blossoms ~5 mm across. Matelea has relatively showier green flowers with distinctive surface patterns. The fruit test is just as valuable: smooth inflated talayote pod versus rough/studded Matelea follicle.

field_matrix.talayote: Usually many tiny ~5 mm flowers on a racemelike axillary spray
field_matrix.matelea: Fewer, much showier 5-lobed flowers with conspicuous face markings

field_matrix.talayote: Pale green with thin whitish margins; 3-lobed corona segments
field_matrix.matelea: M. reticulata strongly netted/silvery center; M. edwardsensis mostly lengthwise lined/bell-shaped

field_matrix.talayote: Opposite and cordate, may be quite large
field_matrix.matelea: Opposite and cordate too; not a stand-alone separation

field_matrix.talayote: Inflated, relatively blunt, smoothly surfaced ~7.5–9.5 cm

comparison_cards.caution: Both groups can have WHITE latex and heart-shaped opposite leaves, and share milkweed floral architecture. Don't identify from sap/leaf shape alone.

comparison_cards.title: Talayote or anglepod?
comparison_cards.look_here_first: When the plant is fruiting, check whether the pod is simply PLUMP and SMOOTH (talayote) or sharply LONGITUDINALLY ANGLED while smooth (anglepod). When flowering, tiny pale green-white many-flowered sprays support talayote; large uniform olive-green star flowers support anglepod.

field_matrix.talayote: Smooth broadly inflated, not sharply five-angled
field_matrix.anglepod: Smooth with conspicuous sharp longitudinal angles
Relatively large (regional ~16–25 mm) uniform olive-green flower stars

comparison_cards.caution: The shared name 'milkweed vine' or leaf form cannot identify either.

study_strategy.warning: Do not generalize white latex to Cynanchum laeve; within North American FNA key talayote white latex vs C. laeve clear latex.

visual_comparison.title: Talayote is not a pearl milkvine
visual_comparison.subtitle: Authentic exact-species talayote photograph sources are linked, not copied. Compare these existing Matelea learner photographs with the talayote original-site studies until photo-specific licensing is pinned.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: Tiny green-white axillary sprays and PLUMP SMOOTH pod = TALAYOTE. Large green NETTED star + SILVERY PEARL = Matelea reticulata. Green striped HAIRY BELL = Matelea edwardsensis.
